newsitem.title: UK: UK auction result good but not stunning-analysts.
newsitem.headline: UK auction result good but not stunning-analysts.

text.p: The Bank of England achieved a respectable level of cover in Wednesday's auction of 25-year gilts but the result was unlikely to spur much movement in the long end of the curve, analysts said.

"It was perfectly adequate but it's not going to set the world on fire," said Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Kleinwort Benson. "But people who were expecting it to go really well will be a bit disappointed. The long end is not going to race ahead."
The auction of 2.5 billion stg of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021 was covered 1.93 times with a price tail of 3/32 and a yield tail of one basis point.
The March long gilt future edged lower in the wake of the auction. By 1119 GMT it was 6/32 weaker at 112-29, compared with 113-01 before the auction.
Stephen Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking, called the result "very good".

"The cover is good for this maturity," he told Reuters Financial Television. "To get 1.93 cover is pretty good going, even though the amount, at 2.5 billion stg, is rather small compared to some of the three billion issues we have seen a year ago."
Michael Dicks, UK economist at Lehman Brothers, said the yield tail of one basis point was a sign the auction went well.
The lowest accepted price at the auction was 106.28, while the highest was 107.03.

"We marked the 2021s at 107.06 last night so the market had built in a concession to the stock to get the thing away, and sure enough it's gone with relatively good cover," said Mark Capleton, international bond strategist at BZW.

"There's always a bit of uncertainty about long-dated auctions because clearly for market-makers there's a risk involved, so you're really reliant on good ultimate investor demand and we seem to have got it."
The previous auction of 25-year gilts in September was covered 1.73 times with a yield tail of two basis points and price tail of 6/32.
"The cover was higher than last year and, perhaps more importantly still, the tail has been squashed down to one basis point," Dicks said.
Scott at Kleinwort said the cover was reasonable for an auction of long-dated stock. "Traditionally auctions of longs attract less cover than mediums or shorts so it's perfectly adequate," he said.
Analysts said the gilt market would now turn its attention to Wednesday's Humphrey Hawkins testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
